BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: There is an increasingly complex set of risks — such as geopolitical tensions and wars, energy price volatility, trade uncertainty, large global fiscal deficits and elevated asset prices.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Economy was resilient in Q1 but uncertainties mounting. Dimon explicitly declined to forecast recession: "I'm not forecasting anything, I'm simply saying, for JPMorgan, we have to be prepared for a recession, and that you can have stagflation."
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Consumer and business credit sound; card originations moderated deliberately. Loan growth modest, mortgage flat. Provision build continues as late-cycle caution mounts despite Q1 resilience.
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: Card NCO ~3.3% Q1, FY26 guide 3.4%. Card spend volumes +8% YoY. Mortgage delinquencies at low end of historical range. Dimon on credit cycle: "if there's a credit cycle, I do expect it will be worse than people think relative to the scenario."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Dimon (Q1 press release): While we cannot predict how these risks and uncertainties will ultimately play out, they are significant and they reinforce why we prepare the firm for a wide range of environments. Fed on hold; stagflation flagged as a prepared-for scenario, not a forecast.
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: On cyber, Dimon (Q&A): "has made it worse, it's made it harder." — JPM is testing Anthropic's Mythos model and noted it "does create additional vulnerabilities. And maybe down the road, better ways to strengthen yourself too." Dimon has publicly framed AI efficiency gains as likely to be competed away across banks, with benefits accruing to customers rather than industry margins. JPM spends ~$2B/yr on AI.
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: Card NCO ~3.3% in Q1; FY guide 3.4%. Provisions rose YoY on card credit. Mortgage delinquencies still at low end of historical range. Dimon cautious on consumer late-cycle risks despite Q1 resilience.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: FY26 NII trimmed $1.5B to ~$103B (all markets NII revision; non-markets held flat). Expenses ~$105B. Markets revenue record $11.6B (+20%) — FICC $7.1B (+21%), Equities $4.5B (+17%). IB fees +28% YoY, #1 on Dealogic.

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: The NII that we're generating is going to drop to the bottom line, that continues to be our position. Equities had their best quarter ever with revenues up 30% year-over-year.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Moynihan (prepared): "the macro backdrop remains constructive" and "We see the forward look of GDP growth rates in the U.S. in the 2% range," "Credit performance remained stable and consistent with our expectations." Continued healthy client activity through Q1.
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Moynihan: "The U.S. consumer continues to spend " On CRE: "improved results in CRE office loans" with "no new inflows of nonperforming assets into office exposures,"
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: Moynihan: "debit and credit card spending was up 6% year-over-year. This total is about 25% of the way consumers spend money " Total net charge-offs "were approximately $1.4 billion with a net loss rate of 48 basis points."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Moynihan: "the ongoing conflicts in the Middle East, including implications for the energy market inflation and growth" remain watch items — "we continue to watch them carefully." FY26 NII growth guide raised: "we're raising our full year NII growth guidance range for 2026 versus 2025 to be up 6% to 8%,"
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Moynihan: "we've got 90 installations working, all 200,000 teammates have access to AI or can use it every day." Headcount "down about 1,070 people from year-end 2025 through attrition," Separately (Mar 2026 press coverage, not on earnings call): BofA deployed an AI advisory platform built on Salesforce Agentforce to ~1,000 financial advisers.
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: Total NCO rate 48 bps in Q1. CRE office losses continuing to improve. Consumer credit broadly stable with resilient spend.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: FY26 NII guide RAISED to +6–8% (from +5–7%). Q1 NII +9% to $15.9B. Operating leverage +290bps. Equities trading record revenues +30% YoY. ROTCE 16% (+200bps YoY).

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: With revenue growing faster than expenses, pre-tax, pre-provision profit grew 14% from a year ago.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Scharf: "at this point, it is likely there will be some economic impact based on what has already occurred, but there are both risks and potential mitigants, so it is hard to predict the ultimate impact." Consumer "remains resilient in the aggregate but increasingly bifurcated beneath the surface."
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Scharf: "Upper-income consumers continue to benefit from elevated equity prices, home equity, and cash buffers accumulated earlier in the cycle, allowing discretionary spending to remain firm. By contrast, lower-income households are more exposed to higher interest rates and energy prices." Loans +11% YoY; deposits +7%.
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: "our net charge-off ratio was stable from a year ago at 45 basis points." Consumer NCO "increased modestly from the fourth quarter to 78 basis points " New credit card account growth "nearly 60% from a year ago, driven by higher digital and branch-based openings." Scharf on Home Lending: "We are very comfortable with the plan we have in our Home Lending business today, which is focusing on people who are broader clients within the bank."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Scharf: "We have managed credit well over many cycles and are well-positioned to support our customers and navigate a variety of economic scenarios." "we returned 5.4 billion dollars to shareholders in the first quarter, including 4 billion dollars in common stock repurchases," FY26 NII reaffirmed ~$50B.
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Scharf (Q1 call): "Fargo, our AI-powered virtual assistant, reached over 1 billion customer interactions less than three years since its launch." "we are increasing our investments in areas like technology, including AI, as well as in advertising, while continuing to execute on our efficiency initiatives which has resulted in 23 consecutive quarters of headcount reductions."
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: NCO total 45bps — stable. Provision $1.135B (up YoY). Average loans +11% to $996B; deposits +7% to $1.4T. CET1 10.3%. Credit quality stable.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: FY26 NII reaffirmed ~$50B (±). Revenue $21.45B missed $21.77B consensus on NII stagnation; shares fell ~5%. All segments grew: Consumer +7%, Commercial +7%, Wealth +14%. Returned $5.4B (incl. $4B buybacks) to holders; CET1 10.3%.

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: Services, our crown jewel, had an exceptional first quarter. Markets crossed $7 billion in revenues for the first time in a decade. We remain well on track to deliver the 10% to 11% ROTCE for the year.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Fraser: "One good first quarter does not a full year make. The first quarter is always the strongest, and we do have an unclear macro environment ahead." "North America from greater resiliency than other parts of the world face given the macro environment and the conflict in the Middle East."
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Services new mandates +40%, revenues +17%. Cross-border transactions +12%, deposits +16%, AUC/AUA +20%. Four of five core businesses reported double-digit revenue growth.
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: Fraser (prepared): "total U.S. Cards NCL rate of between 4% and 4.5%, which is lower than the aggregate of the expectations that we provided previously for Branded Cards and Retail Services, reflecting the delinquency trends and loss performance we have seen year to date."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Fraser: "we are focused on driving sustainably improving returns over time, not just short-term upside." FY26 ROTCE target 10-11% reaffirmed; Q1 delivered 13.1%. Longer-term returns to be laid out at Investor Day.
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Fraser: "We are methodically deploying AI at scale across the firm and strengthening our defensive capabilities, and you will be hearing much more about this on Investor Day."
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: Card delinquencies stabilizing. Consumer resilient. Services — crown jewel — new mandates +40%, revenues +17%. Cross-border txns +12%, deposits +16%, AUC/AUA +20%.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: Q1 ROTCE 13.1% · Revenue +14% · EPS $3.06 beat $2.64 est. Markets >$7B for first time in 10 years — FICC $5.2B (+13%), Equities record $2.1B (+39%). Net income $5.8B (+42% YoY). Laying out longer-term returns at Investor Day.

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: Goldman Sachs delivered very strong performance for our shareholders this quarter, even as market conditions became more volatile. Our clients continue to depend on us for high quality execution and insights amid the broader uncertainty, and we remain confident in how we've positioned our businesses. The geopolitical landscape remains very complex — so disciplined risk management must remain core to how we operate.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Solomon: "the geopolitical landscape remains very complex, and the ultimate impact of higher energy prices on inflation and growth is yet to be determined." Q1 saw rising volatility tied to the Middle East conflict.
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Consumer banking fully exited. Total loan portfolio $253B at quarter end — focus is institutional/wholesale. Institutional credit quality performing.
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: No consumer card exposure. All lending is wholesale/institutional. Solomon: "if the resolution of the conflict drags, that probably will be a headwind in some of these areas particularly inflation trends as we get further into the second and the third quarter."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Solomon: "the environment for investment banking activity continues to be incredibly robust, particularly M&A activity." On IPOs: "there is no question that with the conflict in the Middle East, IPO activity slowed a little bit, particularly in March." Advisory revenues "rose 89% year-over-year on higher completed volumes." $6.4B returned to shareholders.
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Solomon: "we are also investing for long-term growth, including through One Goldman Sachs 3.0" — "accelerating our investments in cloud migration, and in the accuracy, completeness and timeliness of our data. These investments are critical to optimizing the deployment of AI solutions "
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: Consumer banking fully exited. Total loan portfolio $253B (growth in corporate/collateralized). Institutional credit focus.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: Q1 revenue $17.2B, EPS $17.55, ROE 19.8%. Advisory revenues $1.5B (+89% YoY). Equities net revenues record $5.3B. $6.4B returned to common shareholders (incl. record $5B repurchases + $1.4B dividends).

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: The U.S. consumer remained healthy, overall economy remained resilient through the first quarter. We still expect our earnings power on the other side of the Discover integration to be consistent with what we expected at the time we announced the deal, inclusive of the Brex and Hopper travel infrastructure.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Fairbank: "The unemployment rate improved slightly in the quarter despite some high-profile headlines about layoffs... Income growth continued to run ahead of inflation. Consumer spending remained robust."
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Fairbank: "we continue to really feel very good about not only our portfolio performance, but good for the credit outlook of consumers" and the "opportunity to continue to lean in to origination and credit line growth in our business." NIM 7.87%.
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: Fairbank: "the domestic card business posted another quarter of top line growth and strong credit results." "On a sequential quarter basis, our charge-off rate moved in line with the seasonality" and "our delinquencies improved relative to what we would expect from normal seasonality."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Fairbank: "if energy prices remain elevated for an extended period of time, that would be a real headwind for consumers and probably a drag on the overall macro economy." Provision includes "about $3.8 billion of net charge-offs and an allowance build of $230 million."
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Fairbank: "All companies will be able to take advantage of AI, but the leverage is vastly greater when AI is embedded in the company's ecosystem... Our entire technology is architected to enable these capabilities at scale embedded in our modern ecosystem." "We now fully own the technology that we have built in partnership with Hopper and the Hopper talent we've worked with will join Capital One."
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: Provision $4.1B · $3.8B net charge-offs + $230M allowance build. Excluding Discover, card volumes +8% YoY. Consumer macro resilient. Pleased with Discover's credit policies, bullish on bringing Discover onto COF tech/credit platform.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: Q1 adj EPS $4.42 MISSED $4.61 est.; adj revenue $15.23B missed $15.37B. NIM 7.87%. Brex acquisition closed April 7. Debit customers converted to Discover Network. Net income $2.2B (+57% YoY).

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: We had a very strong start to the year. Revenue in the quarter grew 11%, or 10% on an FX-adjusted basis, and EPS was $4.28, up 18% over the prior year. Card member spending grew 10% on a reported basis — the highest quarterly growth in three years.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: "Card Member spending grew 10% on a reported basis, and this is the highest quarterly growth in three years, driven by strong growth across both goods and services and T&E." Premium cardholder base largely insulated from macro headwinds; T&E leading growth.
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Primarily a charge card/short-term revolving issuer. Write-off rates stable at historically low levels, delinquency flat. We really haven't seen any pull forward at all... from a consumer perspective, we see no pull forward at all on tariff-driven buying.
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: We continue to see strong demand and engagement with our premium products. Within our U.S. Platinum portfolio, we are seeing accelerated spend growth following the refresh, while maintaining high retention rates after the fee increases went into effect.
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: If you think about our consumers, what they tend to do is they spend a little bit less, revolve a little bit less in a downturn — but that scenario is not visible in Q1 data. FY26 EPS guide reaffirmed $17.30–$17.90. NFL deal announced.
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Acquired Hyper, an AI-powered expense management startup backed by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman — deal expected to close Q2 2026. Hyper will be integrated into Center, AXP's expense management platform. Squeri introduced Amex Agentic Commerce Experiences (ACE), a developer kit to embed AXP cards into AI-powered transactions. AXP and Hyper previously partnered in 2024 on the Hypercard Rewards AmEx card.
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: Credit quality remains best-in-class. Write-off rates stable / low. Delinquency flat. Provision reflects loan growth, not deterioration.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: FY26 REAFFIRMED: revenue +9–10%, EPS $17.30–$17.90. Platinum refresh driving accelerated spend with high retention post fee increase. Globally 70%+ of new accounts on fee-paying products. Gen Z/Millennial and premium travel (+T&E) leading growth. NFL deal announced.

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: Synchrony Financial started the year with strong momentum and delivered first quarter financial results that included record first quarter purchase volume of $43 billion, reflecting the enduring appeal of Synchrony Financial's multiproduct suite.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Doubles: The macro environment is still pretty constructive... you have some watch items. We are watching inflation very closely, higher gas prices, other factors that I think are creating some uncertainty out there with consumers. "But they really seem to be looking past it at this point. We do not see it impacting spend."
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Wenzel (prepared): "Our first quarter net interest margin increased 76 basis points versus last year to 15.5%," Growth drivers: OnePay, Bob's Discount Furniture, RH, plus "approximately $725 million of Lowe's commercial co-brand loan receivables, which was added in early April."
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: NCO 5.42% Q1 — improved from 6.38% prior year. Doubles: "We expect delinquency and losses to follow normal seasonality through the year, with net charge-offs peaking in the second quarter." FY26 NCO guide below long-term 5.5-6.0% target range. Record $43B Q1 purchase volume.
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Higher NIM from repricing a significant EPS driver. New partnerships de-risk concentration risk. FY26 EPS guide: Synchrony "remains on track to deliver between $9.10 and $9.50 in diluted earnings per share,"
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Doubles: we do not want to be adding headcount right now. We want to drive productivity through the tools... how we drive AI into all aspects of our business to drive a flat headcount environment and get leverage. On Agentic Commerce: Agentic commerce is going to fundamentally change how consumers discover new products, how they research, read reviews, and ultimately purchase... the purchase actually gets completed inside of the AI platform.
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: NCO 5.42% in Q1; FY26 guide below 5.5-6.0% long-term target. Payment rate +50bps vs prior year. Delinquency / allowance stabilizing.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: FY26 EPS $9.10–$9.50. Q1 EPS $2.27 adj (+20% YoY). NII $4.64B · NIM 15.5% (+76bps). Receivables mid-single-digit growth FY. OnePay, Bob's, RH ramping; $725M Lowe's commercial added April. Record $43B Q1 purchase volume.

BANK_COMMENTARY.quote: We are committed to positive operating leverage and to having it driven more by revenue growth as we look into 2026. Continue to grow our fee categories — we want to be known for a heavy fee mix driving strong returns.
BANK_COMMENTARY.economy: Kedia: "the macroeconomic backdrop remains constructive, despite some softening of sentiment recently. Consumer spend, core loan demand, and credit delinquency trends all indicate relative stability." Stern: another record on the consumer deposit side, +$7B YoY.
BANK_COMMENTARY.lending: Kedia: "Net interest income on a taxable equivalent basis increased 4.1% year over year, supported by robust core loan growth " On card: "new products aimed at affluent transactors, along with significant increases in marketing, have resulted in double-digit growth in account acquisitions over the past four quarters "
BANK_COMMENTARY.cards_loans: NCO 0.56% — well below card-heavy peers. Fee income +6.9% YoY across payments, capital markets, and wealth. Kedia: "What I will add on sentiment is it is turning to more core demand, which we find to be very healthy."
BANK_COMMENTARY.macro: Kedia: "there was a real pause pending some resolution or clarity around tariffs." "it is turning to more core demand, which we find to be very healthy." FY26 revenue guide +4–6%, >200bps positive operating leverage.
BANK_COMMENTARY.tech_ai: Kedia: "we are focused on becoming an AI-native organization." ~$2.6B technology investment for 2026 (~15% of revenue). 83% of active customers digitally engaged (vs 80% a year ago). Amazon co-brand partnership — Kedia: "This partnership is unique from traditional co-brand card arrangements in anticipating a clear pathway to broader banking relationships over time."
BANK_COMMENTARY.credit: NCO ~0.56% — well below peers. Credit quality stable across portfolios. Provision moderate.
BANK_COMMENTARY.outlook: Q1 EPS $1.18 (+15% YoY), revenue $7.3B (+4.7%). NII +4.1% YoY; fee income +6.9% YoY. FY26 revenue +4–6% with >200bps positive operating leverage. Heavy fee mix focus — payments + capital markets + investment services momentum.

MACRO_STATE.verdict: Mixed signals across the four pillars.

phases.source: FRED GASREGW · EIA weekly retail gasoline
phases.status_reason: Gasoline +$1.16/gal (+39%) vs pre-shock baseline — well beyond $0.50 confirmation threshold. Expected window: weeks 0–2.
phases.commentary: Retail pumps moved within ~2 weeks of the WTI spike; +$1.16/gal pass-through is roughly in line with the $0.24/gal-per-$10/bbl rule-of-thumb.

phases.status_reason: Decelerating vs pre-shock pace (-4.1% < 5.3%). Inflation phases only confirm on acceleration.
phases.source: FRED CUSR0000SAS4 · BLS CPI Transportation Services (monthly)
phases.detail: Jun'26 457.169 vs 458.772 prior · post-shock +-4.1% ann. · pre-shock 6-MMA +5.3%
phases.commentary: Transport Services running at pre-shock pace — oil shock not yet visible in the monthly cadence.

phases.status_reason: Decelerating vs pre-shock pace (-50.6% < 6.2%). Inflation phases only confirm on acceleration.
phases.base_effect_note: YoY jumped 0.4% → 15.5% (+15.1pp), but this is largely a base effect: Jun'25 index 276.558 was a local dip. Monthly pace is what matters.
phases.detail: Jun'26 vs prior month · post-shock +-50.6% ann. · pre-shock 6-MMA +6.2%
phases.commentary: CPI Energy tracking oil gently — passthrough slower than expected.

phases.status_reason: Decelerating vs pre-shock pace (2.8% < 4.2%). Inflation phases only confirm on acceleration.
phases.source: FRED CUSR0000SEFV · BLS CPI Food Away from Home (monthly)
phases.detail: Jun'26 vs prior month · post-shock +2.8% ann. · pre-shock 6-MMA +4.2%
phases.commentary: Restaurant prices decelerating slightly — menu changes typically lag oil by 3–5 months, so the first real test will be May–June prints.

phases.source: FRED CPILFESL · BLS CPI ex-Food & Energy (monthly)
phases.status_reason: Core CPI 2.57% vs 2.5% pre-shock (+0.1pp) — within the ±0.5pp noise floor for Core CPI YoY. Expected window: weeks 20–32 (months 5–8 post-shock), currently at week 21.
phases.note: Core CPI at 2.57% — energy input costs tracking
phases.commentary: Manufacturing/chemicals absorb input costs over 5–8 months. Too early for this phase — energy input costs only began passing through in Mar'26 PPI.

phases.source: UMich Survey of Consumers (direct) · prelim mid-month, final end-of-month
phases.status_reason: UMich dropped from 56.6 to 54.4 (-2.2pt). Confirmation threshold: 0.5pt move. Expected window: weeks 2–6, currently at week 21.
phases.note: UMich at 54.4 — post-shock reading confirms decline
phases.commentary: Sharp drop in visible-inflation-sensitive households. Pump pain + media cycle around oil shock drove the print. UMich often overshoots relative to actual spending changes.

phases.source: FRED PSAVERT · BEA Personal Saving Rate (monthly, ~1-mo lag)
phases.status_reason: Saving rate 3.0% vs 4.5% pre-shock (-1.5pp). Expected window: weeks 8–16.
phases.commentary: Saving rate compressing as expected — liquid buffer erosion underway.

phases.source: NY Fed Household Debt & Credit Report · CC 90+ DPD (quarterly)
phases.status_reason: Latest CC 90+ DPD is quarterly (NY Fed HHDC), reading 2026-01-01. Pre-shock. Expected window: months 5–10 (weeks 20–40). First post-shock look is Q3'26 release (~Nov'26).
phases.note: CC delinquency at 2.92% — pre-shock data, too early
phases.commentary: 90+ DPD is quarterly (NY Fed HHDC) and lags 2–3 quarters. Current reading is pre-shock; first real look is Q3'26 release (Nov'26).
